answer: Give each identity a stake released only in a ripple of small slices as it accrues real history, so cloning pays per head. Score every account through a prism of independent metrics — response coherence, peer links, timing — and treat lockstep accounts as one ridge of the same mountain: when a cluster trips the similarity threshold the whole ridge forfeits its unvested deposit. The marginal clone is cheap, but exposure is group-wide, so farming cost scales with swarm size.
